items.title: Euro futures hit 1.5-year lows on strong U.S. economic data.
items.excerpt: Dan Deming analyzes the latest price action in the FX markets, highlighting the Euro's decline to a 1.5-year low. Euro futures face continued selling pressure, dropping in nine of the last 11 sessions, driven by robust U.S. economic data. Deming notes that solid GDP and ISM figures reinforce the strength of the U.S. economy, supporting the dollar in a higher interest rate environment. This dollar strength is creating broad headwinds across the currency complex, with the British Pound and Australian Dollar seeing pronounced weakness, while the Japanese Yen and Canadian Dollar post more modest losses.

items.title: Why higher yields are hurting everything except AI
items.excerpt: Higher bond yields are already hurting much of the equity market, even as AI-led megacap tech keeps the S P 500 looking resilient. Key points: The S P 500 is hiding the damage. Technology and communication services are keeping the index afloat, while most other sectors are falling. Higher yields are hitting rate-sensitive sectors first. Utilities and real estate face higher refinancing costs and stronger competition from bonds, while financials are starting to feel tighter credit conditions. AI remains the market s shelter for now. Strong earnings and balance sheets are helping mega-cap tech withstand higher yields, but that leaves the broader market increasingly dependent on a narrow group of winners. items.title: British Pound futures rise on Bank of England rate expectations.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino analyzes the recent performance of British Pound futures, which formed an inside range day to finish higher against the U.S. dollar. Despite U.K. fiscal concerns and the 30-year gilt yield climbing to its highest level since 1998 ahead of the October 28 autumn budget, expectations for further Bank of England tightening continue to support the currency. Traders now look ahead to upcoming speeches from Monetary Policy Committee member Catherine Mann and Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey for signals on a potential November rate hike.

items.title: Surging Treasury yields and Fed minutes put markets on watch.
items.excerpt: Treasury yields enter the week in focus after the 2-Year yield surged 54 bps and the 5-Year jumped 61 bps in September. Focus turns to Wednesday's FOMC minutes, which will detail the central bank's first rate hike since July 2023, as market probability of an October move has fallen to 24%. Meanwhile, the unofficial start of a new earnings season arrives with 12 companies holding market caps over $1 billion scheduled to report, including Pepsi and Delta Air Lines. Traders also monitor an economic calendar featuring global PMI data, U.S. Jobless Claims, and the Michigan Consumer Sentiment reading.

items.title: Euro FX futures slide to 16-month lows as dollar finds support.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures extend their decline for a fourth consecutive session, falling roughly 0.75% to 1.1274 and marking their lowest levels since mid-May 2025. The selloff is primarily driven by sustained strength in the U.S. dollar, which remains near the top of its recent range despite a downward shift across the Treasury yield curve following comments from Federal Reserve officials. Additional pressure on the euro stems from ongoing inflationary and energy-related concerns in the eurozone heading into the winter months. Broad dollar strength is also weighing on other major currencies, with the British pound sliding toward its lows for the year and the Australian dollar facing renewed pressure, while the Japanese yen remains bound within its multi-month range.

items.title: Q4 Outlook for Investors: Raise the bar
items.excerpt: Our Q4 base case is a volatile upward grind, but with much greater dispersion beneath the index. Key points: AI meets expensive money: AI spending can remain strong, but higher funding costs, rapid obsolescence and rising reinvestment needs will increasingly separate companies that can comfortably finance the AI race from those spending simply to stay competitive. Inflation needs more than one hedge: Oil is only part of the risk. El Ni o, fiscal spending and the AI infrastructure buildout could also keep pressure on food, power, commodities and bond yields. Bonds are competitive again: With the US 10-year Treasury yield around 5%, investors no longer need to rely as heavily on equities for returns. items.title: Euro futures drop 2.5% as markets look to jobs data.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures continued to decline through the end of September, closing out the month with a loss of over 2.5%. The currency struggled as sustained dollar strength pushed prices to a new year-to-date low close, settling at 1.1330. As prices have moved lower, the CVOL Index has indicated steadily rising volatility across the market. Looking ahead, traders turn their focus to the labor market, with Thursday's Challenger job cuts and jobless claims leading into Friday's critical nonfarm payrolls report.

items.title: Australian Dollar futures hit 2-month low as Fed maintains hawkish tone.
items.excerpt: Dan Deming examines the FX markets as Australian Dollar futures face heavy selling pressure, dropping 0.5% to hit a two-month low around the 0.6975 level. He discusses the macroeconomic themes driving the broader currency complex, including the Federal Reserve's hawkish tone on interest rate trajectories, which continues to provide strong support for the U.S. dollar. Deming also notes similar multi-month lows across Euro and British Pound futures.
